messages.subject: changing prioritization while in queue ?
parts:
Is it possible to change an arrival's prioritization while in queue for a resource? 

Have a heavily used resource with a constant stream of low, medium and high priority arrivals. Due to the number of medium and high priority arrivals, low priority arrivals are not accessing the resource resulting in unrealistic wait times. Wishing to change low priority arrivals to medium priority after a certain wait time for the resource.

Thanks,

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] changing prioritization while in queue ?
parts:
2018-04-23 16:12 GMT+02:00 <david.j...@gmail.com>:
> Is it possible to change an arrival's prioritization while in queue for a
> resource?

Enqueued arrivals are inactive by definition, and cannot perform any
action. You can set a reneging condition though, change the priority
and retry.

Consider for instance the following simulation:

t <- trajectory() %>%
seize("res") %>%
timeout(2) %>%
release("res")

simmer() %>%
add_resource("res") %>%
add_generator("high_p", t, function() 1, priority=1) %>%
add_generator("low_p", t, at(3)) %>%
run(20) %>%
get_mon_arrivals()

The low_p arrival, at 3, will never take the chance to seize the
resource, because there is always a new high_p arrival that takes the
front of the queue. But

t <- trajectory() %>%
renege_in(
5,
out = trajectory() %>%
set_prioritization(c(2, 2, FALSE)) %>%
rollback(2) # back to "renege_in"
) %>%
seize("res") %>%
timeout(2) %>%
release("res")

simmer() %>%
add_resource("res") %>%
add_generator("high_p", t, function() 1, priority=1) %>%
add_generator("low_p", t, at(3)) %>%
run(20) %>%
get_mon_arrivals()

Now the low_p arrival reneges at 8, increases its priority and
retries. It has to wait another unit of time for the server to be
available, but now it is in the front of the queue and takes the
server at 9.
